title: E-ZPass: higher tolls, but what improved?
premise: E-ZPass is electronic toll collection, not one national company: each toll authority sets rates and controls an account program, customer-service and payment vendors, and road capital projects. I-PASS is Illinois' interoperable toll collection program. Price and service trends must be scoped to the exact operator and jurisdiction.
method: Separate toll rate and fee, E-ZPass discount, observed billing accuracy, collections, customer service, and infrastructure outcomes.
Never call a proposed rate, projected revenue, contract value, authorization or earmark an observed collection or completed upgrade.
An audit sample from one interchange or time period does not measure the overall E-ZPass error rate.
Uncollected tolls represent an agency revenue/collection problem, not an additional household toll charge.
Neither a billing mistake nor a revenue increase proves corruption or a specific toll increase was caused by misconduct.
Report when a proposed project, adopted contract or toll increase has no completed-project or rider time-savings data.

agencies.name: NY State Thruway · E-ZPass
agencies.scope: New York Thruway, not Port Authority or MTA crossings
agencies.verdict: Audit found generally accurate billing but meaningful exceptions and weak controls.

prices.name: 2024 tolls and fees collected
prices.description: Total Thruway toll and related revenues. Includes changes in traffic, tolls, payment and fees; not a toll-rate measure.

prices.name: 2021 tolls and fees collected
prices.description: Earlier nominal revenue comparison, not an inflation-adjusted or traffic-adjusted price series.

outcomes.name: Incorrect or missing tolls at interchange 25A
outcomes.details: About 44,286 of 889,000 transactions appeared inaccurately billed, including about 36,000 incorrectly charged and about 8,000 that should have been charged but were not.
outcomes.limitation: This is NOT a statewide error rate; it includes both mischarges and missed revenue.

outcomes.name: Transactions initially unbillable
outcomes.details: 91,703 transactions from roughly 22.4 million sampled were initially classified unbillable, including unreadable plates.
outcomes.denominator: ~22.4 million transactions in a three-week sample
outcomes.limitation: Not the number of drivers overcharged and not a 2026 estimate.

outcomes.name: Non-revenue tags lacking support
outcomes.details: Eligibility support was missing for 46 of 75 sampled non-revenue E-ZPass tags.
outcomes.limitation: Missing documentation does not establish ineligibility or fraud by 46 drivers.

outcomes.name: Toll-payer advocate case discretion
outcomes.details: In 20 sampled fee-related advocate cases, 12 fee reductions exceeded guidance without documentation supporting the exception.
outcomes.limitation: Procedural control issue; not proof that these drivers paid too much.

delivery.name: E-ZPass toll share
delivery.details: E-ZPass represented about 95% of tolls collected, according to state audit.

delivery.name: Road quality versus revenue growth
delivery.details: No verified common-year segment-level pavement, bridge condition and delay trend has been joined to the revenue growth.

money: Contracted tolling technology, image processing, mailing and receivables collection
Toll payer advocate and resident-discount eligibility controls
next: Reconcile toll invoice against crossing, plate, vehicle class and account state
Publish incorrect-charge rate by facility and month
Publish reversed violations, disputes, average resolution time and fee waivers
Join funded Thruway segment projects to completion and road-condition changes

rights.label: NY Thruway Office of the Toll Payer Advocate
rights.note: If the tag fails, contact the account-issuing customer service center and preserve account/plate records.

agencies.name: MTA Bridges & Tunnels · E-ZPass
agencies.scope: MTA toll crossings; excludes Port Authority NJ–NY crossings
agencies.verdict: Prior audits showed significant image-based toll collection leakage; current per-crossing correction and infrastructure return need matched data.

prices.name: 2020 operating revenue
prices.description: TBTA total operating revenue, not an E-ZPass fee or local bridge price. Helps fund regional transit.

outcomes.name: Unbilled tolls in past audit
outcomes.details: NY State Comptroller reported more than 6 million unbilled tolls after open-road tolling rollout.
outcomes.denominator: Multi-year tolling operations; not the number of unique motorists
outcomes.limitation: Historical collection leakage, not an observed 2026 error rate.

outcomes.name: Estimated lost toll revenue
outcomes.details: Auditors estimated unbilled transactions caused $55.7M in toll revenue leakage during the examined period.
outcomes.limitation: Estimated uncollected money is NOT extra charges paid by drivers or proof a fare was raised.

delivery.name: November 2024 E-ZPass usage
delivery.details: MTA board report lists E-ZPass NY and non-NY account transactions at 85% across bridge and tunnel facilities.

delivery.name: Crossing-specific time savings or completed repairs
delivery.details: Needs facility capital project completions and audited pre/post travel times, not agencywide MTA subway OTP.

money: Operating and maintenance costs for bridges and tunnels
Transit subsidy funded by bridge/tunnel operations
Capital repairs, bridge and tunnel renewal
next: Track share of E-ZPass transactions by bridge and tunnel
Disclose unreadable tags and erroneous invoices corrected per month
Compare collection contractor cost with verified recovered receivables
Link crossings to completed bridge/tunnel capital repairs and travel-time results

rights.label: MTA tolls and violations support
rights.note: Toll bills and E-ZPass violations may be managed in a separate portal from the E-ZPass account.

agencies.name: Port Authority crossings · E-ZPass
agencies.operator: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
agencies.scope: GWB, Lincoln/Holland tunnels, Staten Island Port Authority bridges
agencies.verdict: CPI-linked toll adjustments and extra processing charges are documented; crossing-specific delivered benefits still need verification.

prices.name: Peak E-ZPass CPI increment
prices.description: Additional annual inflation-based toll increment authorized under prior board policy; not the full toll rate.

prices.name: Fixed toll adjustment
prices.description: Part of previously authorized fixed annual additions through 2028. Exact tag/crossing rate depends on payment method and class.

outcomes.name: Tag read/payment processing surcharge policy
outcomes.details: Port Authority says added adjustments encourage use of E-ZPass and properly positioned transponders to offset processing/collection costs of unread tags.
outcomes.denominator: Applies under toll schedule rules; no common percentage inferred
outcomes.limitation: A policy rationale is not independently verified per-transaction processing cost.

delivery.name: 2026–2035 capital plan
delivery.details: Port Authority's capital plan covers airports, ports, bridges, tunnels, PATH and more; not E-ZPass spending or a facility-level improvement.

delivery.name: Crossing-specific road reliability
delivery.details: Need completed bridge/tunnel renewals, pavement condition, closure frequency and travel-time reliability.

money: Facility toll revenue and operating costs
E-ZPass account and license-plate back-office administration
Debt financing and cross-facility capital projects
Port Authority wider system including ports, airports and PATH
next: Track full toll price by year, account state, tag read and peak status
Publish amount and frequency of unread-tag adjustments and reversals
Track every crossing's repairs as completed rather than approved
Publish customer complaints and case resolution median time by facility

rights.label: Port Authority E-ZPass tag and Toll Bill help
rights.note: A transponder that misreads can lead to a mailed bill. Account ownership depends on the issuing agency; confirm the issuer before disputing.

agencies.name: Illinois Tollway · I-PASS / E-ZPass
agencies.scope: Illinois Tollway system and interoperable E-ZPass, not CTA fares
agencies.verdict: 2024 transactions and project budgets are documented; verified user-level billing-error and improvement outcomes remain incomplete.

prices.name: Discount for I-PASS accounts
prices.description: I-PASS customers receive 50% off Illinois Tollway standard toll rates; account status, facility and vehicle class still matter.

prices.name: 2024 toll revenue
prices.description: Total Illinois Tollway revenue from tolls in 2024, approximately level with 2023; not proof that an individual's price stayed flat.

outcomes.name: Electronic toll share
outcomes.details: Illinois Tollway annual report says 86.2% of toll transactions were paid using I-PASS/E-ZPass.
outcomes.limitation: Usage share is not billing accuracy, toll affordability or infrastructure outcome.

delivery.name: 2026 bridge/pavement/fleet maintenance
delivery.details: Program budgeted for existing-system bridge, pavement, facilities, fleet maintenance and safety improvements.

delivery.name: 2026 electronic tolling upgrades
delivery.details: Budgeted for toll plaza and electronic toll collection system upgrades; not proof of successful deployment.

delivery.name: Billing dispute / service resolution
delivery.details: Need refund counts, disputed charges upheld/reversed, I-PASS tag failures and median resolution time over time.

next: Use actual toll plaza and vehicle class to compare payment methods
Get quarterly dispute reversals, refunds and unreadable-plate rates
Follow 2026 $62.6M toll-system program from budget to executed contracts and acceptance testing
Compare pavement, travel times and safety before and after completed projects

rights.label: Illinois Tollway I-PASS customer service
rights.note: I-PASS works at supported E-ZPass road facilities; current sticker tags are free when ordered directly from Illinois Tollway or received at its service center.

crossNetwork.title: Account issuer matters
crossNetwork.description: An E-ZPass tag may be issued by New York Thruway, Port Authority, MTA, New Jersey, or another member agency. Dispute a failed tag with the issuer rather than assuming the crossing operator owns the account.

crossNetwork.title: A toll bill can be a different system
crossNetwork.description: E-ZPass account activity, violations and Tolls by Mail bills may appear in separate portals; confirm the issuing agency and never pay unsolicited scam links.

crossNetwork.title: Public promises need delivery evidence
crossNetwork.description: Agencywide capital budgets can be large while one bridge or tunnel sees little immediate visible change; compare physical projects and service on the facility actually used.

crossNetwork.title: Payment method changes the toll
crossNetwork.description: Account state, correctly read tag, vehicle class, peak/off-peak and direction may change rates. Illinois I-PASS is interoperable but has its own program benefits.

missingSeries: Per-facility annual E-ZPass toll rates, gross and net of discounts
Correct-charge and incorrect-charge rates by toll plaza, time and vehicle class
Customer refunds, violation waivers and median time-to-resolution by issuer
Disputed debt and collections costs separated from recovered toll principal
Contracted readers, vendors, transaction costs and amendments by provider
Capital projects completed and physical bridge/road-condition change per facility
Reliable travel-time change and road closures by crossing
Publicly reported lobbying, donations and conflicts tied to specific awarded vendors

sources.label: New York State Comptroller's 2025 Thruway audit
